newsitem.title: MONGOLIA: Mongolia firms needs 32,000 T of wheat imports.
newsitem.headline: Mongolia firms needs 32,000 T of wheat imports.

text.p: Mongolia's biggest wheat company, Altan Taria, said on Thursday it needed to import 32,000 tonnes of wheat that it could not source domestically.
"We are falling short of 32,000 tonnes of wheat," Altan Taria manager Tsedev said in an interview. "We are planning to buy it from abroad to fulfil our production."
The company, which supplies 30 percent of Mongolia's flour, had not yet decided where to buy the grain.
Altan Taria had sourced only 28,000 tonnes on the domestic market of the 60,000 tonnes planned for this year because of a poor harvest, he said.
The main reasons for the small harvest were late sowing because of huge fires and a drought in the spring and a fall in the area under grain, Tsedev said.
Other companies had also complained of a shortage of grain.
The Moeron Guril mill in northern Hoevsgol province said it had collected only 3,500 tonnes of wheat, far short of a planned 6,000 tonnes this year.

The company would have to close its mill for 10 months from December this year because of the shortage of grain. The mill needed 15,000 tonnes of wheat to fulfil its annual capacity to produce 10,000 tonnes of flour.
The Selenge Guril mill in northern Selenge province said it has been able to find 24,000 tonnes of grain, against the 64,000 tonnes the company needed in the year to produce 45,000 tonnes of flour.
